phases.title: Establish the foundation
phases.description: Ownership, access, security and the implementation baseline.

phases.title: Connect the facility
phases.description: Stripe setup and operator onboarding before live payments.

phases.title: Onboard the member
phases.description: Payment-first enrollment, document upload and authorized access.

phases.title: Book and manage resources
phases.description: Availability, automatic confirmation, exceptions and changes.

phases.title: Run the kitchen session
phases.description: Timed reminders, individual check-in, safety and exit.

phases.title: Bill and reconcile
phases.description: Recurring memberships, usage charges, collection and recovery.

phases.title: Maintain compliance
phases.description: Renewal, expiry reminders and booking eligibility.

phases.title: Monitor the environment
phases.description: Flavors-only Swift Sensors integration and historical visibility.

phases.title: Communicate and administer
phases.description: Publishing, operator tools and controlled account changes.

phases.title: Understand operations
phases.description: In-app facility dashboards and separate B Street analytics.

phases.title: Validate and release
phases.description: End-to-end acceptance, controlled go-live and recovery.

phases.title: Operate and evolve
phases.description: Repeat daily operations, retain history and separate future scope.

nodes.title: Reconcile the project baseline
nodes.summary: Apply the latest email decisions over the older scope.
actions: Replace QuickBooks references with Stripe throughout schema and flows.
Record the nine Phase 1 modules and the new billing/booking decisions.
rules: Flavors is the pilot; a standalone multi-client product remains Phase 2.
Stripe Connect is configured for the platform model without assuming the entire Phase 2 application is included.
checks: Every original module has a destination in this map.
No QuickBooks connection or customer mapping remains.

changes.before: Phase 1 included read-only QuickBooks visibility and no payment gateway.
changes.after: Client explicitly replaces QuickBooks with Stripe billing, then adds Stripe Connect. Flavors remains the pilot; the standalone multi-client platform remains the Phase 2 goal.

nodes.title: Activate accounts and environments
nodes.summary: Use the supplied Microsoft accounts and Stripe invitation.
actions: Verify assigned rights, service connections and access to test resources.
Enable tenant/site guest sharing and a site-level app catalog.
rules: Subscriptions and account details have been provided; access still needs testing.
B Street hosts the tenant and owns Avenue.
checks: Deploy a sample web part and read a test list.
Confirm service-account ownership without putting credentials in code.

changes.before: Tenant owner was unspecified and Business Premium was assumed.
changes.after: B Street HQ owns/hosts Avenue and purchases licenses. Business Basic ×3, Power Automate Premium ×1 and Power BI Pro ×1 are the stated build setup; account details were later confirmed supplied.

nodes.title: Model identities and permissions
nodes.summary: Separate platform, facility, member business and team-member access.
actions: Map each identity to its member/facility and authorized role.
Keep payments, files and checklist answers private; expose only agreed calendar fields.
rules: B Street is super-admin; Flavors has an operator and a restricted staff account.
Only the Flavors owner may override expired-document or overdue-balance booking blocks.
checks: Member A cannot fetch B’s private record by direct URL/API.
Restricted staff cannot perform owner-only overrides.
nodes.exception: If permission setup fails, keep private records inaccessible and queue repair.

changes.before: Generic member, operator-admin and super-admin tiers; up to two operator admins.
changes.after: B Street retains super-admin access and can assign support staff. Flavors gets one operator and one restricted staff account; only the Flavors owner can override overdue-balance/expired-document booking blocks.

nodes.title: Configure the facility catalog
nodes.summary: Load plans, bookable spaces, equipment and operating settings.
actions: Create plans with included hours and extra-hour rates.
Configure stations, equipment, storage and the clarified event/dining resources.
rules: Plan tiers affect allowances and rates.
Exact prices, resource capacities, checklist questions and grace periods still need supplied configuration.
checks: Validate representative member plans and prices with the operator.
Use the facility timezone for booking and billing boundaries.
nodes.exception: Do not invent missing rates or timing values.

changes.before: Plans, resources and rates were requested but booking limits were not established.
changes.after: Plans include different hour allowances and tier-specific extra-hour rates. Provide membership prices, equipment/storage charges and resource configuration; B Street will onboard the initial members for January billing.

nodes.title: Create the two interfaces
nodes.summary: Keep members in the browser and staff in the admin app.
actions: Build responsive member web parts and role-aware navigation.
Build operator/staff screens with shared authoritative data and workflows.
rules: No member-facing Power Apps app or Power Pages.
No custom native app; member journeys run in desktop/mobile browsers.
checks: Test a real guest browser session and phone layout.
UI visibility never substitutes for record-level authorization.

changes.before: Members and staff both use the Canvas App.
changes.after: Manager recommends SharePoint pages with custom web parts for members, retaining the Power Apps admin app for staff. The client’s later replies proceed on this approach.

nodes.title: Establish trusted integration endpoints
nodes.summary: Privileged operations run outside member browser code.
actions: Select and approve server-side execution for Stripe operations and HTTPS webhooks.
Validate callers, store secrets securely and record idempotent operations.
rules: SPFx must not contain Stripe secrets or sensor credentials.
Existing subscriptions do not prove that backend hosting and every premium flow are covered.
checks: Reject forged requests and incorrect signatures.
Document costs and ownership before activating any extra service.
nodes.exception: Backend host and credential-storage implementation remain unselected.

nodes.title: Review Stripe Connect responsibilities
nodes.summary: Confirm the platform’s direct-charge SaaS configuration.
actions: Inspect fees, refunds, disputes, verification and negative-balance settings.
Document which party handles each responsibility and flag platform exposure.
rules: B Street/Avenue should not receive or hold client payment funds.
Do not promise zero platform liability solely because direct charges are used.
checks: A payment is created on the test connected account.
Client receives payouts; any platform-risk setting is reviewed.
nodes.exception: Do not enable a setting that changes funds routing or liability before approval.

changes.before: No payment gateway; invoices and balances came from QuickBooks.
changes.after: Avenue/B Street is the Connect platform. Facility clients connect their own Stripe accounts; direct charges and payouts belong to the facility. Review all fees, refunds, disputes, losses and verification responsibilities; flag possible B Street exposure before enabling.

nodes.title: Launch Stripe-hosted operator onboarding
nodes.summary: A facility operator connects its own payment account from Avenue.
actions: Authenticate the authorized operator and start Stripe onboarding.
Stripe collects financial and verification information directly.
rules: Do not collect/store the client’s Stripe password, secret key, bank details or verification documents.
An Avenue invitation can be forwarded; generate Stripe’s short-lived onboarding link after authentication.
checks: Expired/used links safely regenerate for the right operator.
Return to Avenue does not alone prove verification is complete.
nodes.exception: Resume incomplete onboarding without duplicating the facility connection.

changes.before: Facility Stripe account onboarding was not part of the original scope.
changes.after: Launch Stripe-hosted client-account onboarding from Avenue. Do not collect/store the client’s Stripe password, secret key, bank details or verification documents. Provide the operator invitation only after test approval.

nodes.title: Verify account readiness and events
nodes.summary: Keep Avenue aware of payment capability and onboarding status.
actions: Verify event signatures and resolve the correct connected account.
Retrieve current account capability/requirement state when necessary.
rules: No cross-facility event or payment data leakage.
Process repeated/out-of-order events safely.
checks: Successful, incomplete and failed onboarding states display correctly.
Replay does not duplicate changes.
nodes.exception: Unverified events are rejected; failures go to an operational queue.

changes.before: Only scheduled QuickBooks invoice/balance synchronization was described.
changes.after: Test that a client connects, payment status returns to Avenue and the payment appears under the connected account.

nodes.title: Demonstrate the test flow
nodes.summary: Show the exact operator experience and a simulated payment.
actions: Connect a test facility, create a test direct payment and return its status to Avenue.
Show account records, funds routing and the responsibility findings.
rules: No live onboarding or live payment processing before explicit approval.
checks: Client sees the actual onboarding screens and test account payment.
Open responsibility questions are resolved before release.

changes.before: No Stripe demo or payment go-live approval gate was specified.
changes.after: Demonstrate the completed test flow and exact client-facing onboarding. Confirm platform settings and responsibilities, obtain approval, then proceed to the real operator/live flow.

nodes.title: Select plan and payment date
nodes.summary: Capture the member’s business and selected membership.
actions: Present membership plans and the approved prices.
Let the member choose a monthly collection date from the 1st through 15th.
rules: New members pay before operational onboarding begins.
No public or unapproved applicant document uploads.
checks: The selected plan/date are associated with the correct applicant.
First-payment amount and proration follow an agreed rule.
nodes.exception: Initial payment, approval ordering and rejected-application handling need final rules.

changes.before: Prospective member supplied details, selected membership and uploaded initial documents before staff approval.
changes.after: Members pay before onboarding starts; select a recurring collection date between the 1st and 15th. No public/unapproved document uploads. First-payment and invoice-cutoff calculations still need decisions.

nodes.title: Complete initial membership payment
nodes.summary: Stripe handles the payment under the facility’s connected account.
actions: Calculate the charge from trusted plan data.
Confirm successful payment through verified Stripe status.
rules: Never trust a browser-supplied price or success flag.
Store Stripe references and necessary status, not payment-card data.
checks: A failed or abandoned payment does not activate full member access.
A repeated request cannot create duplicate charges.
nodes.exception: Payment failure offers an approved retry path; do not grant operational access.

changes.before: Avenue did not collect payments; payment stayed in QuickBooks.
changes.after: Use the facility’s Stripe billing/payment setup for the initial and recurring membership payment. Successful payment initiates member onboarding.

nodes.title: Start authenticated onboarding
nodes.summary: Collect the member’s operational profile after payment.
actions: Provision the permitted guest/onboarding access and capture member details.
Link member business, authorized team and paid plan.
rules: B Street will onboard current members for January billing.
A paid state alone does not establish that every compliance requirement is complete.
checks: Paid members reach their own onboarding area.
Another applicant cannot access their profile or documents.
nodes.exception: Staff approval after payment is not conclusively resolved in the trail.

changes.before: Application/documents came before approval and access provisioning.
changes.after: Only paid new members and current members enter onboarding and upload after login. B Street handles initial member onboarding. The exact remaining manual approval step is still unresolved.

nodes.title: Upload permits and compliance files
nodes.summary: Documents are collected only after authenticated onboarding starts.
actions: Upload required files with document type and issue/expiry dates.
Apply member-specific permissions and track required/missing documents.
rules: No public Microsoft Forms upload journey.
Final document types, warning window and validation requirements must be configured.
checks: Direct download denies other members.
Staff on-behalf upload grants the correct member access.
nodes.exception: Failed upload or permission grant remains pending; do not label it compliant.

changes.before: Initial documents were submitted through an external application form before full access.
changes.after: Collect documents only from current members or paid new members after login/onboarding begins. Public document upload is not wanted.

nodes.title: Evaluate operational eligibility
nodes.summary: Expose the member’s portal once the applicable requirements are satisfied.
actions: Evaluate paid membership and required compliance state.
Show clear status and what needs attention.
rules: Booking blocks apply for expired documents and overdue balances.
Only Flavors owner may override those specific blocks, with audit.
checks: A blocked member cannot bypass checks through direct requests.
Owner override is explicit and attributable.

nodes.title: Browse the shared calendar
nodes.summary: Members see kitchen occupancy without private operational data.
actions: Read the requested calendar range and filter resources.
Display member name, station, equipment, date and time.
rules: Private files, balances, answers and contact data do not belong on shared rows.
checks: All allowed bookings in the range appear, including beyond local row limits.
Private data never leaks through shared-list access.

nodes.title: Submit a reservation
nodes.summary: Request station/equipment and a start/end interval.
actions: Validate membership, compliance, balance and resource constraints.
Calculate allowance usage and applicable pricing under agreed rules.
rules: Plan limits and overage rates affect the request.
Booking mutations and price calculations require authoritative validation.
checks: Reject invalid duration, inaccessible resources and forged ownership.
Evaluate booking eligibility again at commit.
nodes.exception: Exact capacity/buffer and booked-versus-attended usage rules still need confirmation.

nodes.title: Automatically confirm an available booking
nodes.summary: Apply first-come, first-served confirmation for conflict-free requests.
actions: Check station, equipment and date/time conflicts.
Recheck when confirming and record the confirmed reservation.
rules: No manual approval for an eligible conflict-free request.
The original design excludes a database-level lock; the new auto-confirm path needs a tested concurrency strategy.
checks: Simultaneous requests cannot silently create conflicting confirmations.
Confirmed booking appears in the shared calendar.
nodes.exception: Serialize/recheck confirmation or select another approved safe strategy before acceptance.

changes.before: Staff approved or denied every booking; conflicts were flagged for manual resolution.
changes.after: Automatically approve when station, equipment and date/time are available, following first-come, first-served allocation. Send conflicts to staff. Safe concurrent confirmation is an implementation decision, not a client-specified database lock.

nodes.title: Route conflicts to facility staff
nodes.summary: An exception branch handles contested resources or times.
actions: Notify operator/staff of the conflict.
Record resolution and only confirm an agreed available alternative.
rules: A conflict must not silently override another reservation.
checks: Pending conflict is clearly distinguishable from confirmation.
The requestor sees the final outcome.

changes.before: Staff reviewed all reservation requests.
changes.after: Only conflicting requests require staff resolution, subject to the other eligibility rules.

nodes.title: Send confirmation and portal actions
nodes.summary: Member receives a simple booking notice with Avenue links.
actions: Send an approved booking confirmation.
Provide authenticated change/cancel links into Avenue.
rules: The email trail permits booking confirmation wording and portal links.
Permission to send booking notices is not permission to email private wellness or financial details.
checks: Clicking the link opens the authorized booking.
A retry does not cause unintended repeated notices.

changes.before: No operational content in email; generic login-only nudges.
changes.after: Client permits a simple booking confirmation and a portal button to change/cancel and view details. This does not authorize emailing private wellness answers or unrestricted financial details.

nodes.title: Request additional time
nodes.summary: Members, operator and staff can request an extension.
actions: Check the extra interval against other reservations.
Add eligible overage charges and update reminder targets.
rules: Conflicts alert the Flavors owner/staff for resolution.
Extra usage above included credits/storage allowance becomes billable.
checks: A change does not leave stale reminders active.
Member, operator and staff actors are audited.
nodes.exception: The invoice cutoff for late-month extensions is still a billing decision.

changes.before: Developer flow mentioned exit or extend without defining billing and permissions.
changes.after: Member, owner and staff can request extra time when available. Conflicts alert the Flavors owner/staff; excess hours or storage allowances produce additional charges.

nodes.title: Cancel or shorten a booking
nodes.summary: Apply notice windows and controlled adjustments.
actions: Allow kitchen/storage cancellation with 24-hour notice.
Route late requests to owner/staff to decide credit restoration or forfeiture.
rules: Members do not automatically receive unused time back for leaving early.
Owner/staff can adjust the booking and credited hours.
checks: A late request cannot self-grant a refund of credits.
Confirmed changes update availability and billing.

changes.before: No detailed cancellation or unused-hour policy was supplied.
changes.after: Kitchen/storage: 24-hour cancellation notice. Late requests require owner/staff approval and discretionary credit loss/restoration. Leaving early does not automatically restore hours; only owner/staff can adjust the booked time.

nodes.title: Apply event-specific cancellation rules
nodes.summary: Dining/events have different cancellation and refund rules.
actions: Apply the stated 15-day/full-refund and 7-day/forfeit rules.
Record the security deposit and paid amounts when relevant.
rules: For seven-day notice the client says deposit/payments are forfeited with no further amount owed.
Rules for 8–14 days and other unlisted boundaries are not supplied.
checks: Correct notice boundary and authorized refund action are tested.
Refunds follow the connected-account responsibility configuration.
nodes.exception: Do not invent the policy for unspecified notice periods.

changes.before: No separate dining/event cancellation policy.
changes.after: 15+ days: full refund. At seven-day notice: security deposit and payments already made are forfeited with no further balance owed. Unspecified intervals/boundaries remain open.

nodes.title: Handle a no-show
nodes.summary: Booked hours are forfeited unless authorized staff override.
actions: Identify a missed booking under the agreed detection rule.
Record consumed hours and any owner/staff exception.
rules: No-shows lose booked hours.
Owner/staff can override this rule; this is distinct from owner-only debt/compliance overrides.
checks: Exception is auditable and does not double-deduct hours.
nodes.exception: No-show detection timing has not been specified.

changes.before: No-show consequences were unspecified.
changes.after: No-shows lose booked hours. Flavors owner/staff can override.

nodes.title: Run 3 / 2 / 1-hour reminders
nodes.summary: Scheduled reminders prepare members for the booking.
actions: Find eligible confirmed bookings and due reminder events.
Check booking revision, cancellation and member state before sending.
rules: Source flow proposes a 15-minute scan; exact-minute delivery is not guaranteed.
Deduplicate logical events and track ambiguous send outcomes.
checks: Retries and overlapping runs do not blindly resend.
Late-booking catch-up policy is approved.
nodes.exception: Catch-up, grace periods and uncertain-send recovery need configuration.

nodes.title: Check each team member in
nodes.summary: Capture wellness and food-safety answers on arrival.
actions: Resolve the member business and individual submitting the checklist.
Capture answers, question version, identity and timestamp.
rules: Client requires every team member to check in with wellness items.
Individual team-member identity/access model needs completion beyond the original member-only schema.
checks: Answers are private and attributed to the actual submitter.
Duplicate submission rules are applied.
nodes.exception: Exact questions and per-team identity permissions are configuration dependencies.

changes.before: Fixed entry/exit checklist per booking; HTML included wellness while DOCX omitted it.
changes.after: Wellness is explicitly retained, and every team member must check in on arrival so the supervisor can follow up where needed. Individual team identities and exact questions still need configuration.

nodes.title: Notify responsible people of a failed checklist
nodes.summary: Route failures for correction and follow-up.
actions: Alert the Flavors operator/staff and the member business owner.
Track follow-up and corrective action.
rules: The member business remains responsible for its team’s issue.
Facility or another member’s issues are handled by Flavors with the appropriate party.
checks: Only authorized recipients can read the answer details.
Failure detection does not invent an unapproved automatic access ban.
nodes.exception: Detailed safety responses belong in the private portal, not broad emails.

changes.before: Missed checklists escalated to staff; failure handling was not defined.
changes.after: Failed answers notify the member business owner and Flavors owner/staff for correction and follow-up. The member business remains responsible for its team; facility/other-member issues go through Flavors.

nodes.title: Escalate missing check-in
nodes.summary: Detect missing entry after the configured grace period.
actions: Nudge the member, then escalate to staff when unresolved.
Record staff outreach and suppress reminders once resolved.
rules: Grace periods and escalation contacts must be supplied.
checks: No escalation after a valid entry or cancelled booking.
One resolved incident does not repeatedly reopen.

nodes.title: Complete exit and close the session
nodes.summary: Submit the exit checklist or request an authorized extension.
actions: Prompt exit at session end.
Save private exit answers and update session state.
rules: Original scope requires entry and exit checklists per booking.
The trail explicitly expands individual entry; whether exit is per person needs clarification.
checks: Exit cannot silently extend the reservation.
Actual versus booked-hour reporting remains explicit.
nodes.exception: Missing exit routes to staff; never fabricate completion.

nodes.title: Resolve overdue exit and outreach
nodes.summary: Staff handle unresolved end-of-session cases.
actions: Flag a missing exit after the approved interval.
Log one-off staff follow-up and final resolution.
rules: Retain booking and checklist history.
checks: Resolved cases stop generating overdue notices.

nodes.title: Define the invoice cycle
nodes.summary: Resolve calendar-month usage against the chosen debit date.
actions: Define first payment, recurrence anchor and invoice cutoff.
Define late-month overages, proration, plan changes, credits and taxes if applicable.
rules: Client wants payment dates 1–15 and overages added to the month’s invoice.
How usage after that date is collected is not resolved; do not silently choose next-month billing.
checks: Example invoices reconcile for members paying on day 1 and day 15.
Month-end usage has an agreed destination.

changes.before: Read-only financial dashboard; no recurring invoice or collection logic.
changes.after: Generate monthly membership invoices, automatically add approved extra usage, let members select payment day 1–15. The reconciliation between calendar-month overages and that debit date is still open.

nodes.title: Calculate usage and overages
nodes.summary: Translate reservations and authorized adjustments into charges.
actions: Apply included plan hours and approved resource rates.
Account for extensions, cancellations, no-shows and storage/equipment charges.
rules: Avenue calculates charges; Stripe invoices/collects.
Bookable hours versus actual attendance must be agreed.
checks: A booking revision does not double-charge.
Every charge traces to a reservation or approved adjustment.

changes.before: Usage reporting existed, but Avenue did not calculate billable invoice additions.
changes.after: Avenue calculates extra booked hours, equipment and applicable storage amounts, then sends the charges to Stripe for invoicing/collection. Apply plan allowances and authorized cancellations/no-shows.

nodes.title: Create the recurring invoice
nodes.summary: Build membership plus approved extra-charge lines.
actions: Create/update the facility-connected member billing records.
Apply the approved collection date and usage cutoff.
rules: Payment objects belong to the correct facility’s connected Stripe account.
Stripe Billing/API capabilities, fees and exact route need configuration review.
checks: Retry cannot create a second invoice/line.
Invoice matches manually calculated reference examples.

changes.before: QuickBooks supplied existing invoices and balances.
changes.after: Stripe generates monthly invoices and collects recurring membership payments under the facility account; Avenue supplies plan/usage charges.

nodes.title: Collect payment through Stripe
nodes.summary: Automatic collection updates the member’s balance and history.
actions: Track success, authentication-needed and failure states.
Update Avenue from verified events, with source reconciliation.
rules: Funds go to the connected facility; payout timing is controlled by Stripe/account settings.
A browser return page alone cannot mark an invoice paid.
checks: Payment appears on connected account.
Repeat or out-of-order webhooks cannot corrupt the balance.
nodes.exception: Surface failures to authorized users and retry under the agreed policy.

nodes.title: Show invoices and payment history
nodes.summary: Give each member one place for past and upcoming charges.
actions: Show invoices, payments, outstanding balance and upcoming/estimated overages.
Show financial summaries to operator and permitted staff.
rules: Members see only their own data.
B Street analytics can use approved operational financial data without collecting private bank credentials.
checks: Another member cannot retrieve the record directly.
Estimated and finalized charges are clearly distinguished.

changes.before: Members saw own invoices/balances synchronized from QuickBooks.
changes.after: Members see Stripe-based invoices, full payment history, upcoming charges and booking overages inside Avenue. Authorized operator/staff get permitted financial visibility without collecting private banking credentials.

nodes.title: Block booking for overdue balances
nodes.summary: Apply the client’s owner-only override policy.
actions: Update overdue state using the agreed due-date rule.
Block new booking actions and allow an audited Flavors-owner override.
rules: Staff cannot override overdue/expired-document booking blocks.
The email specifies booking blocks, not a physical door-lock integration.
checks: Server-side booking action enforces the block.
Payment reconciliation clears the block when appropriate.
nodes.exception: Failed-payment retry timing and exact overdue boundary need approval.

changes.before: No automatic booking block for unpaid balances was specified.
changes.after: Overdue balances block booking. Only the Flavors owner may override, not staff. Exact overdue timing remains a configuration decision.

nodes.title: Manage refunds and disputes
nodes.summary: Handle adjustments under the reviewed account responsibility model.
actions: Authorize refund requests and track their final status.
Record disputes and inform the designated responsible facility owner.
rules: Cancellation credit restoration is not automatically a cash refund.
Flag any platform liability or fund-flow change before enabling.
checks: Test refund/dispute event handling in the allowed test environment.
Only permitted users initiate financial adjustments.
nodes.exception: Refund authorization and exception procedures need documented ownership.

nodes.title: Review document expiry daily
nodes.summary: Track required documents over the membership lifecycle.
actions: Set Current / Expiring / Expired using configured dates.
Identify missing requirements separately from expired uploads.
rules: Original default warning window is 30 days, still to confirm.
Retain renewal history under an agreed retention policy.
checks: Date-only expiry boundary is consistent.
Status refresh does not send a new reminder every scan unintentionally.

nodes.title: Request and record renewal
nodes.summary: Members or authorized staff replace expiring documents.
actions: Send an appropriate renewal notice with authenticated portal access.
Upload the new document and link it to the superseded version.
rules: Staff on-behalf uploads require actor audit.
Do not delete compliance history without a retention decision.
checks: Private permissions apply to each replacement.
Eligibility reflects the authoritative current document.

nodes.title: Enforce expired-document booking blocks
nodes.summary: Only the Flavors owner can grant a recorded exception.
actions: Recheck compliance when a reservation is submitted/confirmed.
Record owner override reason and scope.
rules: Restricted staff cannot override.
Treatment of already-confirmed future bookings after expiry needs a rule.
checks: UI and direct requests obey the same control.
nodes.exception: Do not cancel existing bookings automatically without an approved rule.

changes.before: Document expiry tracking and renewal nudges only; booking restriction unspecified.
changes.after: Expired documents block booking, with an override available only to the Flavors owner. Treatment of existing future bookings remains open.

nodes.title: Map sensors to facility units
nodes.summary: Use supplied API access without repeating credentials in the map.
actions: Map device IDs to refrigerators/freezers and temperature units.
Configure the approved min/max threshold for each unit.
rules: API access and documentation were supplied; monthly limit is 100,000 calls.
Sensor tracking is for Flavors only in the pilot.
checks: Every displayed tile maps to the correct physical unit.
No secrets appear in frontend bundles, exports or logs.
nodes.exception: Device mapping, limits per endpoint and thresholds still require validation.

changes.before: Swift Sensors API access, documentation, limits and mapping were requested.
changes.after: API access and documentation were supplied with a 100,000-calls/month limit. Flavors is the only sensor-tracked client in the pilot. Unit mapping and thresholds still need validation. Credentials are not included in this artifact.

nodes.title: Poll readings and append history
nodes.summary: Scheduled ingestion maintains current and historical values.
actions: Poll within the API budget; deduplicate source readings.
Store source timestamp and update the latest value per unit.
rules: Original proposed cadence is 15–30 minutes, subject to actual API limits.
Calls depend on endpoints, pagination and retries, not just sensor count.
checks: Duplicate polls do not duplicate history.
Reading time and retrieval time are distinguishable.
nodes.exception: Rate limits trigger bounded retry; outages remain visible.

nodes.title: Display temperatures and history
nodes.summary: Show latest synchronized readings with range and freshness.
actions: Display units, source timestamp and Normal / Out-of-range status.
Provide authorized historical views and stale/unavailable indications.
rules: Swift Sensors retains real-time breach alerts.
Avenue polling is not a replacement real-time alarm system.
checks: A stale normal reading is not presented as current.
Threshold boundaries and units are correct.
nodes.exception: History backfill is conditional on provider API capabilities.

nodes.title: Publish announcements and newsletters
nodes.summary: Staff publish to all members or an approved audience.
tech: SharePoint News / Notices — choose canonical source
actions: Create, publish and update announcements.
Send the approved notification with a portal link.
rules: Audience targeting is not a substitute for permissions on confidential content.
The original News-versus-Notices storage ambiguity must be resolved.
checks: Drafts stay private and publication nudges are deduplicated.
nodes.exception: Choose one authoritative publishing model before implementation.

nodes.title: Manage members, plans and staff access
nodes.summary: Operator controls facility operations without changing platform functionality.
actions: Edit member/plan configuration and assign staff visibility within allowed boundaries.
Support B Street super-admin and delegated representative actions.
rules: Flavors receives one operator and one staff account for the pilot.
Additional accounts are a future commercial option, not unlimited free staff licensing.
checks: Forbidden role/owner changes fail outside the UI.
Plan edits do not silently rewrite historical invoice calculations.

changes.before: Up to two operator-admin accounts with generic plan/member management.
changes.after: One Flavors operator account plus one staff account with selectable permissions. B Street retains full platform administration and may assign representatives; extra staff accounts are a future paid option.

nodes.title: Route support requests to B Street
nodes.summary: Client wants a way to request help or on-behalf changes during the pilot.
tech: Avenue support entry — implementation to confirm
actions: Record a support request and assigned representative.
Audit any action taken on behalf of operator/member.
rules: The email requests ticket submission; no separate help-desk product is selected.
checks: Support users only access assigned/authorized facility data.
nodes.exception: Confirm minimum ticket workflow and Phase 1 acceptance rather than adding a full help-desk product.

changes.before: No dedicated ticket/request workflow in the nine original modules.
changes.after: Client/staff should submit a support ticket to B Street for assistance or on-behalf updates during the pilot. Specific ticket-tool/workflow design is not selected.

nodes.title: Deactivate or revoke Avenue access
nodes.summary: Retain records while stopping new operations and notifications.
actions: Mark inactive, stop eligible nudges and remove Avenue-specific access.
Reconcile private grants and apply the agreed future-booking policy.
rules: Do not delete a guest identity used by other client systems without approval.
Stripe subscription cancellation is a separate decision from login deactivation.
checks: Inactive users cannot create new bookings.
Revocation does not destroy required financial/compliance history.
nodes.exception: Future bookings and subscription termination rules need an approved policy.

nodes.title: Build the Flavors operational dashboard
nodes.summary: Provide facility summaries directly inside Avenue.
actions: Show bookings, utilization, peak hours, capacity, member activity and compliance.
Show financial summaries and outstanding charges according to staff permissions.
rules: Build native operational summaries; do not assume embedding Power BI avoids viewer licensing.
Regular members do not need Power BI access.
checks: Sample totals match source records beyond local query limits.
Do not label a delayed aggregate real-time without a defined freshness contract.
nodes.exception: Metric aggregation and scale need a tested design; no arbitrary local-only totals.

changes.before: Compliance and usage dashboards were assigned to Power BI.
changes.after: Flavors needs facility bookings, utilization, activity, compliance and financial summaries inside the Avenue admin dashboard. Client asks to build these with Power Apps/SharePoint without another Power BI Pro seat if feasible.

nodes.title: Create B Street Power BI analytics
nodes.summary: Platform oversight for the pilot with future expansion kept explicit.
actions: Build revenue, booking, utilization and membership trends.
Prepare a facility-aware model; populate only actual pilot data.
rules: Client prefers one B Street Pro seat plus temporary development licensing if needed.
Other interactive Power BI viewers require appropriate coverage.
checks: Booked hours are distinguished from attended hours.
Monthly financial totals and compliance denominators have approved definitions.
nodes.exception: Cross-location reports do not imply unapproved delivery of Phase 2 facilities.

changes.before: Power BI audience and final seat count were unresolved.
changes.after: Power BI primarily serves B Street’s business/platform analytics. Start with one B Street Pro seat plus temporary development coverage if needed. Ordinary members do not use Power BI.

nodes.title: Keep personal summaries in the member portal
nodes.summary: Members review their own reservations, invoices and balances.
actions: Present personal operational and financial history.
Link back to permitted booking and renewal actions.
rules: No member Power BI deployment.
No member-facing Power Apps license-dependent screen.
checks: Personal records are complete, scoped and clearly timestamped.

changes.before: Member own-account views existed, but report distribution was unresolved.
changes.after: Members see individual reservations, invoices and balances directly in Avenue, not in Power BI.

nodes.title: Test every role and failure path
nodes.summary: Validate the system as real guests and staff, not just a developer account.
actions: Run paid enrollment → documents → booking → entry/exit → usage billing.
Exercise conflicts, restricted accounts, failures, refunds and API outages.
rules: No cross-member file/payment/checklist exposure.
Test concurrent auto-booking and retry-safe financial/event processing.
checks: Operator summaries and B Street reports reconcile to reference examples.
Phone browser journeys and direct-access denials pass.

nodes.title: Obtain client test approval
nodes.summary: Review the Stripe demo and the complete pilot acceptance results.
actions: Show the exact operator Stripe onboarding and payment flow.
Document responsibility settings, outstanding rules and release readiness.
rules: No live Stripe activity before approval.
The email requests late-December training and January launch; readiness must be validated, not assumed.
checks: Approval is attributable and specific to the tested configuration.
nodes.exception: If critical access or financial-integrity issues remain, keep test mode.

changes.before: Generic UAT and handover; no explicit Stripe live approval gate.
changes.after: Client must approve the test onboarding/payment experience and responsibility configuration before live Stripe activation.

nodes.title: Connect the real operator and activate production
nodes.summary: Use approved live configuration and a controlled first run.
actions: Send an Avenue start/invitation link for the operator.
After authentication generate Stripe onboarding, verify readiness, then enable approved live operations.
rules: The forwarded link is not a raw reusable Stripe Account Link.
No secret keys, banking data or verification documents enter this artifact.
checks: Verify the first approved live event in the correct account.
Pause schedules safely if verification fails.
nodes.exception: Live setup requires the correct mode-specific credentials and explicit approval.

changes.before: No connected-account production setup or operator link handoff.
changes.after: After approval, provide secure operator onboarding access and confirm the live account configuration. A forwardable Avenue invitation is the proposed safe implementation; the client asked for a secure onboarding link.

nodes.title: Train operator and hand over ownership
nodes.summary: Teach daily workflows and exception handling.
actions: Demonstrate bookings, checklists, compliance, billing issues and owner-only exceptions.
Deliver artifacts, configuration inventory, connection owners and recovery instructions.
rules: No unconditional eight-week or launch-date guarantee from this map.
Build identities and production operator permissions need deliberate handover.
checks: A designated owner can resolve failed jobs and reconnect services.
Restore/rollback rehearsal does not lose records or resend payments.

changes.before: Approximately eight-week sequence, starting when prerequisites and advance are in place.
changes.after: Client requests operator training in the week of December 27 before a January 1 launch. This is a requested milestone, not evidence that a revised schedule has been validated.

nodes.title: Monitor failures and reconcile sources
nodes.summary: Keep integrations and scheduled work observable.
actions: Review failed flows, stale sensors, unmapped records and incomplete provisioning.
Reconcile payment status; replay safely and track API budget.
rules: Never log secrets or broadly expose wellness answers.
Avenue is not an emergency response or physical access-control system.
checks: A duplicate event or replay does not charge twice.
Failures have a named operational owner.

nodes.title: Maintain security and recoverability
nodes.summary: Manage document/sensor history and account lifecycle over time.
actions: Review private grants, service credentials and projected list/permission growth.
Apply approved retention, archive and recovery procedures.
rules: Retention periods and support/warranty terms are not supplied.
A saved app version alone is not proof of full data recovery.
checks: Historical invoices and compliance records remain available as required.
nodes.exception: Agree retention before deleting history or claiming legal compliance.

nodes.title: Separate future platform expansion
nodes.summary: Keep the long-term multi-client product distinct from the pilot.
actions: Capture lessons from Flavors and proposed school/client needs.
Plan facility isolation, configurable feature access and future AI separately.
rules: Standalone multi-client platform, broader rollout and AI are aspirations in the trail.
Stripe’s multi-client capability is not proof those application features are delivered.
checks: New-client functionality is assessed before it is promised.
nodes.exception: This node records future scope; it is not a committed Phase 1 deliverable.

changes.before: A full multi-client platform was deferred to Phase 2.
changes.after: Client reiterates a future standalone configurable platform, mentions a potential school client and future AI, while using Flavors to learn. These are future directions, not automatically delivered Phase 1 features.
